Allanore, A. (2015). Features and Challenges of Molten Oxide Electrolytes for Metal Extraction. Journal of The Electrochemical Society 162(1), E13-E22. https://doi.org/10.1149/2.0451501jes

Locators are printed journal pages (E13-E22; PDF page 1 is an IOP cover sheet; E13 = PDF page 2, so PDF page = printed number - 11). A perspective/review on molten oxide electrolytes: the only technology-level number for iron is the estimated 3700 kWh/t Fe electricity for a practical MOE process (2600 kWh/t thermodynamic minimum, 90% faradaic and 60% thermal efficiency assumed), loaded with temperature 1600 degC and zero process CO2. Other-values: minimum energy, assumptions, 1.85 t CO2/t Fe comparison, historical manganese MOE (Sadacem 6000 kWh/t Mn) and lab faradaic efficiencies. Not loaded: electrolyte property data (conductivity, solubility, viscosity), Fig. 4 bar values (read from chart).
